clips.title: A better editing workflow starts with the source, rather than a pile of generated claims.
clips.text: A better editing workflow starts with the source, rather than a pile of generated claims. First choose complete caption ranges. Keep every word inside the selected range in its original order. Then inspect the sentence before and the sentence after the cut. Look for explanations and qualifications. If the next sentence changes the claim, include it or choose a different clip. Captions should use the new clip timeline. A clip starting two minutes into a recording still needs captions near zero.

review_flags.message: Contains numbers. Confirm their units and qualifications against the original source.

context_before.text: Delete the first two words and the instruction now says the opposite.

context_after.text: Every exported caption should point back to its original source cue. Editors need a trace, not a confident guess.

clips.title: A short video can repeat every word correctly and still tell the wrong story.
clips.text: A short video can repeat every word correctly and still tell the wrong story. The mistake is often not an invented sentence. It is the sentence left outside the cut. Consider this invented editing example. A creator tries a new workflow on one practice recording. Removing dead air cut a ten minute editing pass to six minutes. But that result came from one practice session, not a controlled comparison. The number is useful context, not a promise about how much time everyone will save.

review_flags.message: Contains numbers. Confirm their units and qualifications against the original source.

context_after.text: Another trap is dropping a tiny word that carries most of the meaning.

clips.title: A transcript fingerprint lets another editor check whether the supplied transcript has changed.
clips.text: A transcript fingerprint lets another editor check whether the supplied transcript has changed. However, a matching fingerprint does not prove the transcript matches the audio or that its claims are true. No lexical rule can guarantee that a cut preserves every nuance. Context checks are reminders, not a substitute for judgment. A useful workflow ends with real files: a playable clip, synchronized captions, and an edit record another person can inspect.

review_flags.message: An included qualification follows the opening quote. Do not publish the quote alone as an unqualified claim.

context_before.text: Every exported caption should point back to its original source cue. Editors need a trace, not a confident guess.

context_after.text: Good automation removes repetitive work without removing responsibility. Shorter cuts should not require a different story.

limitations: Source links verify alignment to the supplied transcript, not truth or completeness.
Context flags use English lexical heuristics; they do not guarantee meaning preservation.
No speech recognition or pretrained generative model is included.
The source video is not fingerprinted by the browser and must match the imported transcript.
